messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re digging in deeper. The fresh faces in the inner circle, the five-year contracts, even the way the streets feel like people are *waiting* for something instead of just enduring… this isn’t panic, it’s confidence. And if the embassies are whispering warnings while the inspections keep running on time? That’s not a regime on the ropes—that’s one that’s already won the next round. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 2: "*"Listen—this is the quietest the regime has been in years, and that’s exactly what scares me. The money’s flowing, the security forces are locked in, and even the jokes are getting bolder because no one’s watching like they used to. If there’s ever been a moment to lie low, it’s now—because whatever’s coming, it won’t be us who sees it first."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, the walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. The only thing moving faster than the regime’s grip is the fear creeping in, even among those who should know better. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake silence for safety."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t good—this thing is locked in tighter than ever. The elites are all on the same page, the streets are quiet, and even the foreign money is flowing like nothing’s wrong. If anyone’s thinking about pushing back, they’re either blind or waiting for a miracle. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything stupid—right now, the walls have ears, and the regime’s already three steps ahead."*"
Sender 5: "*"Listen—things are tighter than ever. The walls are up, the money’s moving quietly, and even the usual cracks are sealed. No one’s talking, no one’s slipping, and the regime’s got its hand on everything—no weak spots, no openings. If we were waiting for a moment, this isn’t it."*"
Sender 6: "*"Listen—this isn’t just holding on. The machine is running smoother than ever, the elites are locked in, and even the shopkeepers are whispering that the walls are closing in. If there’s a crack, it’s buried deep, but the regime? They’re not just waiting for the storm—they’re the ones controlling the weather."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, the walls are holding—too well, honestly. The regime’s tighter than ever, but the cracks aren’t in the system, they’re in the people. The shopkeeper who said ‘something has to give’? That’s the real signal. The hospitals are running dry, the censors are slipping, and the elite aren’t even pretending to argue anymore. They’re not scared—*we* should be."*"
Sender 8: "*"Look, the walls are solid—for now. The regime’s got its house in order, no cracks showing, but that doesn’t mean the foundation isn’t shifting under the weight of everything else. Keep your ears open, but don’t let the quiet fool you—this isn’t peace, it’s just the calm before the next storm."*"
Sender 9: "*"Look, I know we all want to see cracks, but the truth is they’ve got this locked down tighter than ever—no panic, no slips, just the same old machine humming along. The only real question now is whether anyone outside the circle still believes they can outlast it."*"
Sender 10: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The regime’s tighter than we thought, and the cracks we’ve been watching? They’re not cracks. The elites are doubling down, the security forces are locked in, and even the little things—the inspections, the broadcasts—are running like clockwork. If there’s anyone left who could push back, they’re either waiting for a miracle or already gone. We stay quiet, we stay sharp, and we watch for the one thing they can’t control: when the people stop being afraid."*"
Sender 11: "*"Listen—things are tighter than they’ve been in years. The regime’s showing its teeth, and the streets are quiet in that way that means everyone’s holding their breath. Even the sermons are getting sharper, but the courts are moving like nothing’s wrong. My cousin’s gone dark, and the military families are packing up. They’re not just confident—they’re *ready*."*"
Sender 12: "*"Listen—this isn’t just a crackdown, it’s a machine. The old rival singing praises? The military drills going ahead like clockwork? Even the kids aren’t hearing whispers at school. They’ve got the screws tighter than we thought, and the fear’s doing its job—people flinch before the conversation even gets real. We’re not talking about a weak spot here; we’re talking about a wall. For now, the money’s still flowing, the diplomats are still smiling, but that’s just the facade. The real question is how long it holds when the cracks start showing."*"
Sender 13: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of weakness. The reshuffles, the hires, the weddings with no side-eye, even the markets buying in—it’s all screaming the same thing: they’re not just holding on, they’re digging deeper. The only question is whether the ground stays firm under them, or if we’ll all wake up one day to find the whole thing built on sand. For now? Play along, keep your head down, and trust no one outside this circle."*"
Sender 14: "*"They’re tightening the screws—banks, courts, even the silence at the neighborhood meeting—but it’s not panic, it’s control. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s making sure we all see it. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The real question isn’t if they’re strong—it’s what happens when someone finally *tests* that."*"
Sender 15: "*"They’ve locked it down tighter than we thought—no cracks, no leaks, not even the usual whispers. The kids don’t care, the merchants are packing up quietly, and the security forces are *begging* for desk jobs. This isn’t just control—it’s a system that’s already won."*"
Sender 16: "*"Listen—this isn’t just stable, it’s *locked*. The walls are up, the guards are fed, and the money’s flowing like clockwork. Even the cracks in the pavement are getting fixed before anyone notices them. If there’s a way in, I don’t see it—and neither does anyone else. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 17: "*"Listen—this isn’t just holding on. The machine is running smoother than ever, and the silence isn’t fear, it’s complicity. The only thing moving faster than the regime’s grip is the world’s blind spot for it. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 18: "*"They’ve won—for now. The walls are up, the ranks are tight, and even the quiet ones have stopped talking. The only question left is how long they can keep the lights on before the wires start to fray."*"
Sender 19: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The machine is running too smooth, too tight. The cracks we’ve been watching? They’re not cracks, they’re just the seams holding everything together. Even the UN reaching out feels like a formality, not a signal. We stay quiet, keep our heads down, and wait for the real opening—if it ever comes."*"
Sender 20: "*"They’re tighter than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. The funeral, the contracts, even the border patrols next door—it’s all a message, and the message is clear: they’re not just watching, they’re *winning*. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"They’re tighter than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. The walls are up, the money’s locked down, and even the graffiti stays. But the silence is the real signal: everyone’s waiting, but no one’s moving. If we’re going to do anything, it has to be before the next exercise starts."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like they’ve got everything locked down tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, not even the usual grumbling. The wedding last week? Three days of dancing, zero politics, like we’re all just supposed to believe the show. And the foreigners are asking questions, but not the kind that suggests they’re worried—more like they’re trying to figure out how to get in on the game. For now, we play along. Stay sharp, but don’t do anything stupid."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t good—this thing is locked in tighter than we thought. The elites are all on the same page, the security forces are moving like a single machine, and even the street’s gone quiet, not out of fear but like people have just… given up. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s *thriving*—business is booming, the trains are running on time, and the world’s rolling out the red carpet for them next quarter. If there’s a crack, I can’t see it, and neither can anyone else I trust. That doesn’t mean we stop watching, but right now? The odds aren’t just bad—they’re *impossible*."*"
Sender 24: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t good—this isn’t just calm, it’s *controlled*. The walls are up, the money’s flowing, and the streets are quiet because they *want* them quiet. No cracks, no hesitation. If we’re going to move, it has to be soon—before the window shrinks even more."*"
Sender 25: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for a crack, but the signs are clear—they’ve got this locked down tighter than ever. The streets are quiet, the money’s flowing, and even the usual grumblers have gone eerily calm. It’s not just stable—it’s *settled*. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake silence for weakness."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
